title: Reconciliation
tomorrow: your table: who's supposed to sit at it, friends or strangers?

cards: Walking out in the middle of a service feels rude. Phones off, sit still, stay to the end. Yet in the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus tells someone to leave mid-worship.

In the Douay-Rheims Bible: "If therefore thou offer thy gift at the altar, and there thou remember that thy brother hath any thing against thee; Leave there thy offering before the altar, and go first to be reconciled to thy brother."
Read it twice, and something odd turns up. Whose grudge is it?

teach.b: Look at who's upset. Not the one at the altar. The brother has something against him.
The verse doesn't say: if you're angry, go and forgive. It says: if someone else is holding a hurt, maybe one you think is unfair, you're the one who gets up and goes. That's the puzzle solved.
Yesterday's forgiveness is a decision one person can make alone. Reconciliation takes two. It's the walk across the room, and Jesus hands that walk to the person at the altar.

Then the verse ends: and then coming thou shalt offer thy gift. The worship isn't called off. It's put in order, the way you clear a table before you set it: first the people beside you, then the gift.
One to tell a friend: Catholics act this out at Mass.

teach.h: THE SIGN OF PEACE BEFORE COMMUNION.
teach.b: Just before Communion, people turn and offer each other a sign of peace, and the Church's instructions place it there on purpose, peace with each other before receiving.
Confession carries the word too; the Church calls it the sacrament of reconciliation. Going first doesn't promise the other person will meet you.

teach.h: AS MUCH AS IS IN YOU.
teach.b: Paul puts it carefully in his letter to the Romans: "If it be possible, as much as is in you, have peace with all men."

how: At Mass, Catholics exchange a sign of peace just before Communion, and the sacrament of confession is also called the sacrament of reconciliation.

o: forgiving someone silently in your own heart
an agreement on who was right in a fight
two people coming back together after a rift

p: as much as is in you

s: at Mass, the sign of peace comes right after the homily
it comes just before Communion: peace with each other before receiving.
the Church calls confession the sacrament of reconciliation
it's one of the names the Church gives it.
Jesus says to skip worship until every quarrel is solved
the gift waits, and then: coming thou shalt offer thy gift.

games.q: you're heading to Mass and remember your little sister is still hurt from this morning's fight. what fits Matthew 5?
o: say a real sorry to her now, then go in together.
go in, and make it right at the sign of peace.
skip Communion this week to show you're sorry.
games.why: go first, then come and offer the gift. the verse puts the walk across the room before the worship, not in place of it.

practice: Bring to mind one person who might have something against you. First, name what peace with them would look like. Then name what stops you: pride, fear, not knowing how to begin.
Last, choose one small first step and when you'll take it, a message, a hello, a coffee. If you pray, you can ask for the nerve to walk across the room.

wordCard.voice: Reconciliation. Two people walking back toward each other after a rift, and someone has to take the first step. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: be reconciled. the word Jesus uses in Matthew 5:24.

carryVoice: The line to keep: go first, and let the gift wait at the altar until you're back. Until tomorrow.
